title: A different type of AI trading... friends and I would love your feedback
author: _PolyWasp_
selftext:
Hey y'all!

A small group of friends here on the West Coast built **PolyWasp**, a free algorithmic trading platform designed specifically for **Polymarket US**.

We've gotten some great feedback so far, but we're still pretty small, with around 40 active users. We're hoping to get more eyes on the project, hear what people think, and figure out what we can improve.

**Here's what PolyWasp can do:**

* **Build your own trading strategies:** Create custom algorithms from scratch using simple, plain-English rules. Combine as many conditions as you want, including price movements, momentum, market types, timing, entry and exit rules, and more.
* **AI-assisted strategy building:** Use tools like Claude or Codex to help create more advanced strategies, even if you don't know how to code.
* **Prebuilt strategies:** Start with an existing strategy and customize it instead of building everything from scratch.
* **Free paper trading:** Test your strategies against real-time Polymarket market data without risking any money.
* **Automated live trading:** Connect your Polymarket US account and promote your paper strategies to real-money trading when you're ready.
* **Build strategies online:** Our new web-based builder lets you create strategies directly in your browser.
* **Bankroll management:** If you just want a way to manage your bankroll better, but don't want to use Bots or Strategies, PolyWasp is capable of being a centralized bankroll manager. Track and manage your trading capital, limit your exposure, even if you're not running automated strategies. You can still make your own manual picks, manage positions, and mix discretionary trading with automated strategies, all in one place.

**For building and testing, everything is free. No subscriptions, no signup required to build or paper trade, and no coding experience needed. We only require signup and membership if you wish to promote to real money trading.**

We're not claiming to have some magical money-printing bot. The idea is to give people the tools to experiment, build their own trading systems, and test whether their ideas actually work before putting real money behind them.

You can check it out at [**https://polywasp.com**](https://polywasp.com).

We'd genuinely appreciate any feedback, feature requests, bug reports, or even criticism. We're actively developing it and want to build something people actually find useful.

Thanks for checking it out!

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: The paper-to-live promotion path seems like the part worth pressure-testing first. Does PolyWasp replay Polymarket US order-book events, partial fills, and market resolution rules, or does paper trading assume fills from displayed prices? A plain-English strategy produced with Claude or Codex could look sound while silently depending on an impossible fill or ambiguous condition. I’d add a promotion report that shows expected versus executable price, liquidity used, unresolved rule ambiguities, and the maximum bankroll exposure before real-money activation.

replies.author: _PolyWasp_
replies.body:
Paper fills are based on real-time Polymarket US market data, not simply assuming execution at the displayed price. For maker strategies, fills are simulated based on orders crossing the ask, while taker fills account for available liquidity at the ask and whether it can satisfy the requested buy size.

One of the nice parts of the platform is that paper strategies continue running simultaneously with their real-money counterparts, so you can directly compare execution and performance under the same market conditions.

It's not a perfect 1:1 simulation, of course. Paper fills tend to be slightly more favorable because they're not actual resting orders competing for queue position and liquidity. That said, from our own real-money testing, we've found the results track surprisingly closely.

comments.author: koryuken
comments.body:
Why do we need to pay you though? Even when going to real money? All the historical data is available. Backtests can be run with Claude code or other. Barrier to entry is already low... I feel like the pitch just isn't there. What's stopping someone from making a strategy, and then running it outside of your platform?

Not hating, trying to be constructive.

replies.author: _PolyWasp_
replies.body:
There's really nothing stopping anyone from duplicating this platform or doing exactly that. For someone determined, they can do that on their own anytime.

The only distinction I'd like to make is that PolyWasp isn't a backtesting platform. It's a live strategy testing and execution platform. You're testing strategies against real-time Polymarket US market data, simulating actual fills and liquidity, and seeing how they perform in live market conditions without risking money.

Think of it like Alpaca for Polymarket.   
  
We do need to generate some revenue to keep the infrastructure running and continue improving the platform over time, so we've decided to make real money trading the paywall. This allows anyone to build and test for free, experience the platform without any other restrictions. The value is really in the convenience of having everything built and maintained for you. But anyone is absolutely free to build and run their own version!

replies.author: koryuken
replies.body: Cool, thank you. Wish you best of luck!

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: paper fills are where prediction market tools usually flatter people. a lot of those books are only a few hundred dollars deep, so a paper order filling at the shown price would have moved it in real life. does yours walk the book or take the top price?

replies.author: _PolyWasp_
replies.body:
It walks the order book, not just the top price, but it does still make some favorable assumptions. We also have conditions to help mitigate this, like requiring available liquidity at the ask to be X times larger than your order size before entering a position. It's not a perfect simulation, but we're trying to get it as close to real execution as possible. 

They buy condition in the builder is called "Money on the ask", and it allows you to require a minimum $ or unit size within "n" cents of the order size. So if the order is going to be $200, you can require $1000 within 2 cents of the ask, or whatever parameters, to prevent buying into thin order books. 

There are also volume conditions and spread conditions that help mitigate the issue of thin order books.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: walking the book covers most of it. what paper still can't see is the queue: for a resting maker order, whoever was ahead of you at that price fills first, and a paper order never waits in line. so I'd trust your taker results well before the maker ones.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: crossing through is the rule I'd pick too. it'll under-fill a bit, but a paper result that's slightly too pessimistic is a lot easier to live with than one that's too kind.

comments.author: GrouchySpeech7982
comments.body: The bankroll manager framing is underrated - a lot of people don't want bots, they just want discipline. Might be worth leading with that for the less technical crowd. Question: for the AI-assisted building, can someone use the web builder entirely without touching Claude or Codex, or is that a required part of the flow?

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: A paper desk that shows every rule check, each closed trade and the daily calendar, losses included, is the most useful part. In the screenshots, the 15-minute BTC trades are priced around 79 to 91 cents, where one loss (-$82.26) wipes out several wins of $12 to $50, so I'd show the break-even win rate at the average entry price, plus the maker-fill rate and what the unfilled orders would have done. The week of Oct 6 to 11 is only about 430 trades, many on the same BTC window, so the independent sample is smaller than it looks. For markets that resolve on a scheduled release, the Build it Better page at Cymetica is where they rebuild apps like this in public.
